title: TRICARE Select Fee Payments, Delinquency Letters and Disenrollment for Nonpayment
content:
**Rule.** Monthly installments of a **TRICARE Select** enrollment may be paid only through a method the tier accepts for monthly installments; annual and quarterly installments may also be paid by a single card payment or check, and an allotment is available only to a sponsor who draws retired pay. A change of frequency or method takes effect from the next installment period. A payment is applied to the oldest unpaid installment first. When an installment is unpaid on its due date a delinquency letter is issued on the tier's delinquency letter day after the due date. The enrollment is disenrolled for nonpayment only once more than the tier's grace period has passed since the due date of the oldest unpaid installment. A payment inside the grace period cures the delinquency. The disenrollment takes effect on the paid-through date and covers every family member billed through the same fee-bearing enrollment; the family may enroll again at the next open season or after a new qualifying life event, or ask for an Enrollment Reinstatement Review within the tier's reinstatement request window.

## Counting the grace period

- **Clock starts from:** the due date of the oldest unpaid installment, which is the first day of the coverage period that installment pays for, as the fee account shows it.
- **Counting:** calendar days, starting the day after the due date; disenrollment may be processed from the day after the due date plus the grace days, and not on that day itself (30 calendar days on the retiree tiers).
- **Comparison:** strictly more than the grace days must have passed; the boundary day itself does not satisfy it.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, 30-day grace period, letter on day 10)

| Oldest unpaid installment due | Date | Standing |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-01 | 2026-04-11 | delinquency letter issued |
| 2026-04-01 | 2026-05-01 (due date plus 30 days) | still inside the grace period; no disenrollment |
| 2026-04-01 | 2026-05-02 | disenrollment for nonpayment may be processed |

## Paid-through date

The paid-through date is the latest end of a coverage period among the installment charges fully settled by payments posted against them. A nonpayment disenrollment takes effect on that date and covers every family member billed through the same fee-bearing enrollment.

## Points of judgement

- **Order of application:** a payment goes to the oldest unpaid installment first.
- **Cure:** a payment made inside the grace period cures the delinquency.
- **Method change:** a new frequency or method applies from the next installment period, not the current one.
